lines.text: Webb's mirrors wear five wedding rings.
The James Webb Space Telescope has a 6.5 meter mirror.

lines.text: Each segment is coated with gold about 100 nanometers thick.

lines.text: The gold goes on as a vapor inside a vacuum chamber.
Gold is soft, so a thin layer of glass goes over it.
Webb looks at infrared light, which people feel as heat.

post.caption: Webb's mirrors wear five wedding rings. The James Webb Space Telescope has a 6.5 meter mirror made of 18 hexagonal beryllium segments. Each one carries a gold coat about 100 nanometers thick, laid on as a vapor in a vacuum, then covered with a thin layer of glass because gold is soft. Gold reflects about 99 percent of the infrared light Webb studies. All the gold together is about 48 grams, about the gold in five men's wedding rings.
